rank_portability.definition: Within each family, average-rank memory-loss rho scaled to [0,1], predicted in a held-out family by the same trait's mean rank in all other families; baseline=0.5. P values use 9999 within-family blocked permutations.

trait_omissions_with_negative_gain: leaf area per leaf dry mass

absolute_memory_portability_blup.interpretation: Trait identity contains modest transferable information on the log scale. The earlier near-zero portability framing is therefore scale-dependent and should not be retained as the manuscript's central claim.

global_trait_spectrum.interpretation: A reproducible aggregate trait spectrum exists, especially across tree treatments within a fixed trait scale.

direct_cross_family_rank_reversal.definition: For each pair of traits, among families containing both traits, the reversal probability is the probability that two distinct randomly chosen families disagree about which trait has the larger memory-loss rho. Weighted summaries weight by the number of available family pairs.
direct_cross_family_rank_reversal.interpretation: Even on the cleaned log scale, two families disagree on the relative ordering of the same two traits roughly 46-48% of the time for well-represented trait pairs.

measurement_aware_latent_reordering.derivation: For latent rho = intercept + family + trait + system, a within-family two-trait contrast cancels the family main effect. Across two random families, contrast correlation r=sigma2_trait/(sigma2_trait+sigma2_system). Under the Gaussian crossed model, P(order reverses)=acos(r)/pi.
measurement_aware_latent_reordering.interpretation: The direct observed reversal frequencies and the sampling-error-aware latent model converge on the same result: the relative ordering of trait memory is extensively re-ranked across families.

revised_central_interpretation: Trait identity defines a statistically reproducible but weak global spectrum of phylogenetic memory. That spectrum is not a fixed lineage-level hierarchy: lineage-specific re-ranking is so extensive that the relative order of two traits reverses between families nearly half the time. The strongest result is therefore coexistence of a real aggregate trait prior with strong lineage contingency, not absence of trait-level structure.
candidate_claim: A reproducible global spectrum of phylogenetic trait memory coexists with near-half cross-lineage reordering.
hard_nonclaims: Do not claim that trait identity has zero transferable information.
Do not retain the old claim that trait portability is generally absent without specifying raw scale.
Do not equate memory-loss rho with an evolutionary rate.
Do not identify system-specific heterogeneity with a known evolutionary mechanism.
Do not call BIEN rank reordering prospective.
Do not call near-half reversal exact randomness; weak but detectable aggregate trait structure remains.

coarse_grained_hierarchy.pair_population: trait pairs co-occurring in at least 5 families
coarse_grained_hierarchy.definition: Global rank gap is the absolute difference between traits' mean within-family normalized ranks. Reversal is the family-pair-count-weighted probability that two distinct families disagree on which trait has larger memory-loss rho.

trait_pair: leaf area per leaf dry mass
robust_anchor_examples_min_10_families.direction: leaf area per leaf dry mass is more conservative (lower memory-loss rho) in the majority of families
diameter at breast height is more conservative in the majority of families

coarse_grained_hierarchy.interpretation: The global spectrum behaves as a coarse prior: traits far apart on the aggregate spectrum have appreciably more stable ordering, whereas fine distinctions among nearby traits are almost completely re-ranked by lineage context.

robust_partial_order.eligibility: trait pair co-occurs in at least 10 families
robust_partial_order.robustness_rule: same majority direction on S3 and prune-only, with majority consistency >=0.75 on both axes

edges.more_conservative: leaf area per leaf dry mass

robust_partial_order.interpretation: Only a sparse set of coarse pairwise inequalities survives across lineages and tree treatments. The aggregate trait spectrum should be interpreted as a weak partial order rather than a portable total ranking.

functional_module_exploratory.chronology: post-outcome descriptive analysis using the trait modules frozen before the original BIEN memory outcomes
functional_module_exploratory.well_represented_pair_rule: trait pair represented together in at least 10 families

within_module_pairs: diameter at breast height (1.3 m) vs stem wood density
leaf area vs leaf area per leaf dry mass
leaf area vs leaf dry mass per leaf fresh mass
leaf area per leaf dry mass vs leaf dry mass per leaf fresh mass

functional_module_exploratory.interpretation: Frequent re-ranking is not confined to comparisons among functionally disparate trait modules. Well-represented within-module pairs reverse at least as often as between-module pairs in this small descriptive subset. This supports spectrum-wide re-ordering rather than a simple between-module artifact, but the module comparison is exploratory and underpowered.

global_separation_vs_reversal_explorator.chronology: post-outcome descriptive check motivated by the alternative explanation that near-half reversal could be driven only by globally near-tied trait pairs
global_separation_vs_reversal_explorator.pair_population: 16 trait pairs co-occurring in at least 10 families
global_separation_vs_reversal_explorator.interpretation: Trait pairs that are farther apart in the global memory-gradient spectrum tend to retain their ordering more often, especially on prune-only. Thus the global spectrum is informative rather than meaningless. However, even the top quartile of globally separated pairs reverses across families roughly one-third to two-fifths of the time, so large aggregate differences do not define a fixed lineage-level hierarchy.
global_separation_vs_reversal_explorator.hard_nonclaim: Do not describe all pair ordering as approximately random. Reversal is conditional on the separation of pairwise global means.
